title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

text.how-you-fall: You fall like a wave: big, sudden and with a pull that surprises everyone, including you. Im is the ocean, the great river, water that moves and refuses to stay still. You're drawn to people who make life feel bigger, the ones who talk about moving to Lisbon on a whim or who can keep up with your curiosity at 2am. You fall through adventure and ideas. A great conversation is your favorite kind of date. The first phase with you is thrilling: spontaneous trips, deep talks, the feeling of being swept up. The trouble comes when the tide turns into routine. You love freedom, and any whiff of being contained can make you drift. That's not because you don't care. It's because oceans need room. Find someone who swims, not someone who builds a pool.
text.flirting: The way you flirt is effortless and a little hypnotic. You're curious, you ask interesting questions, and you make people feel like the most fascinating person you've met all month. You're great at playful mystery: answering a question with a question, leaving at the right moment, texting something intriguing then going quiet. It's magnetic, and you know it. The risk is that people can't tell if you're serious or just enjoying the current. Also, you might flirt with three people at once, not out of malice but because you genuinely find everyone interesting. If you like someone for real, slow the wave down. Make a plan and keep it. Show up on time. For a person who's used to you drifting, reliability is the most romantic thing you can offer.
text.attachment: Your pattern often looks avoidant, driven by freedom more than fear. You love deeply, but you hate feeling trapped, so you might pull back when things get too close too fast, then return when you've had room to breathe. It can confuse partners who need consistency. You also intellectualize feelings. You'll analyze your relationship like a fascinating case study instead of just feeling it. When you trust someone, though, you're generous, open-minded and wonderfully accepting. You rarely judge, and partners feel free around you. The work is telling people your rhythm before it confuses them. "I need some space sometimes, it's not about you" said early saves everyone a lot of worry. The ocean is less scary when people know about the tides.
text.jealousy: You rarely get jealous in the usual way. You're too busy with your own life to monitor someone else's. When it does hit, it's often about freedom: if your partner seems to have a more exciting life without you, or someone else gets to share an adventure you wanted, you feel a sudden, surprising pang. Your trigger is being left behind or left out. You might react by becoming more distant, as if to prove you don't care, or by planning something big to reclaim the spotlight. Neither helps much. The honest move is admitting it, which is weirdly hard for you. "I wish I'd been there" is a vulnerable, simple sentence. Water can be deep without being cold.
text.red-flag: Yeon has notes: you disappear. Not dramatically, just a little more quiet every week, until your partner is texting into the void. You call it needing space. They call it being ghosted by someone who still lives with them. Second flag: commitment allergy. You love the start of things and get restless the moment it starts to feel like forever. Third: you keep a few currents running. Old flames, interesting strangers, the one who "just gets you." You don't think of it as betrayal, because nothing happened. But keeping doors half open is its own kind of not choosing. Freedom is part of who you are, and it's beautiful. Just make sure your freedom isn't costing someone else their peace.
text.what-you-need: You need freedom and a partner who isn't threatened by it. Someone with their own big life, their own passions and plans, who's happy to have adventures together and also happy when you go off to have one alone. You need intellectual connection. A person who reads, wonders, argues and asks "what if." Boredom is your greatest relationship risk, so someone who keeps surprising you is gold. You also need, though you'd rarely say it, a steady harbor: someone calm and reliable you can always return to. The best match for you doesn't try to hold the water still. They're the shore it keeps coming back to, again and again, by choice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im, you love like the ocean. Big, adventurous, people feel swept away by you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And then the tide goes out and they're standing alone on the beach.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You just need freedom! You never try to change anyone.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also keep three old flames on low heat. Just in case.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Tell them your rhythm early. Tides are less scary when people know they're coming.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Needing space is fine. Vanishing for a week is not "space."

spring.intro: In spring Wood takes the lead, and Water feeds Wood. A spring-born Im Water is a river in flood season, pouring life into everything on its banks. In love you are generous, curious and expansive. You give ideas, adventures and long late-night conversations that change people. The season draws your energy outward, which is lovely for others and draining for you. You can pour yourself into someone's growth and then feel oddly empty, or drift toward the next interesting person when the first one stops being a discovery. Metal, your resource, refills you: structure, commitment, someone with a clear sense of self. Rivers need banks. They are what make the water go somewhere.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Im, you inspired them, mentored them and left. That's a TED talk, not a relationship.

summer.intro: Fire owns the summer, and Water controls Fire. A summer-born Im Water is the sea in August: warm on the surface, working hard underneath. In love you are drawn to passionate, bright, dramatic people, and you spend a lot of energy managing their heat. You cool down arguments, rescue plans and keep everything moving. That can make you feel powerful, and also quietly spent, as if you are always containing something. Water evaporates in summer. Metal, your resource, restores you: a partner with principles, time alone, conversations where you are not the one keeping the peace. Choose love that refreshes you instead of love you have to keep putting out.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Im, you calm everyone's fires. It's okay to want someone who brings you water.

autumn.intro: Autumn belongs to Metal, and Metal feeds Water. An autumn-born Im Water is a river gathering strength from mountain springs: clear, powerful and deeply supported. In love you are confident and free. You want a partner who can keep up intellectually and give you plenty of space, and you can disappear for days into your own currents without thinking it matters. With so much resource behind you, your blind spot is overwhelming the people you love with your intensity, opinions or need for freedom. Wood, your output, channels you into warmth and play. Earth, your controller, gives you a shape. A little structure makes the current feel like an embrace instead of a flood.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Im, 'I need my space' for a fortnight isn't freedom. It's vanishing with good branding.

winter.intro: In winter Water takes the lead, so a winter-born Im is the ocean at its deepest. You love with immense depth, intuition and a slightly overwhelming sense of meaning. When you are in, you are fully in, and you can make a partner feel they are the only person you have ever understood. Doubled Water also brings mood tides. You might go from intensely present to strangely distant without warning, and assume they understand why. Earth gives Water direction, and Fire brings warmth to a cold sea. In love that means consistency and lightness: regular plans, playful dates, explaining your silences before they become stories in someone else's head.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Im, your love runs deep and mostly underwater. Just tell them when the tide goes out.

earth.intro: You were born in the Earth days, Im, when the ground takes command and water meets its banks. Earth controls Water, so in love you swing between wanting freedom and wanting something that holds you. You're generous, curious and full of big ideas for the two of you. The risk is pulling away the moment it feels like a rule. You need a partner who gives you shape without boxing you in. Talk about structure early, so it feels chosen, not imposed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Im, a riverbank isn't a cage. It's how the river gets somewhere.

strength.strong: A strong Im Water is a river at flood level. With plenty of Water and Metal in your chart, you are bold, free-thinking and full of ideas about how love should feel. Partners get swept up in your energy, and sometimes swept along by it. Your blind spot is overpowering with intensity and freedom: changing plans on a whim, dominating with opinions, vanishing when you need space without explaining. You expect them to keep up. Give your current a channel. Make small promises and keep them. Check in before you disappear. Depth feels safest when it is predictable.
strength.weak: A weak Im Water is a stream running thin in a dry season. With little Water or Metal support, you still feel big feelings but lack the reserves to express them steadily. In love you go with the flow too much, letting stronger partners set the course while you quietly adjust. Your blind spot is over-giving your energy to their plans, their moods and their dramas. Then you feel lost, unsure what you even wanted. Protect your alone time like any other commitment. Notice where you are drifting before you get there. The right partner widens your banks.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might hold back until someone else makes the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practicing small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard and feel everything at full volume, whether you show it out loud or keep it behind your eyes. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colors and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practicing clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labeled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard and fast, out loud or in silence. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
